title: Simple visual tests may signal early cognitive decline, study finds
content: A new study published in the journal Brain Sciences suggests that simple visual tests may serve as an early indicator of cognitive decline, a precursor to dementia.
summary: Simple visual tests could be an early indicator of cognitive decline. A new study published in the journal Brain Sciences reported this finding.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study links genetic mutation to axonal defects in rare Parkinson's
content: A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences links a genetic mutation associated with Parkinson's disease to abnormalities in a subset of nerve cells. The research provides insights into the causes of the neurodegenerative disorder. D. James Surmeier, Ph.D., the Nathan Smith Davis professor and chair of neuroscience, co-authored the study. He stated that the findings offer new clues regarding how the disease begins and progresses.
summary: A new study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences found that a genetic mutation linked to Parkinson's disease causes abnormalities in specific nerve cells. The findings provide new insights into how the neurodegenerative disorder begins and progresses, according to co-author D. James Surmeier.
author: Medical Xpress

title: HIV activism offers a roadmap for tackling weight stigma
content: Lessons from the HIV response could accelerate fairer and more effective care for people living with obesity. While HIV and obesity are not mirror images, the HIV activism framework offers a potential roadmap for addressing weight stigma.
summary: Although HIV and obesity are not mirror images, lessons from the HIV response could accelerate fairer and more effective care for people living with obesity.

title: Study finds opioid use can become long-term following surgery
content: Claes Gedda of the Department of Clinical Sciences at Danderyd Hospital, Karolinska Institutet, investigated the prevalence of continued opioid use among Swedish patients following surgery. While opioids are effective for managing severe post-surgical pain, prolonged use carries risks of dependence and overdose. Gedda’s thesis examined which patients face a higher risk of long-term usage and evaluated whether opioid use after major surgery can be reduced.
summary: A thesis by Claes Gedda at Karolinska Institutet investigated how common it is for patients in Sweden to continue using opioids after surgery. The research also examined which patients are at higher risk and whether usage following major surgery can be reduced.

title: Oil prices drop to lowest since August after Trump says Iran war is over
content: Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes Business live – latest updates Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end.
summary: Brent crude fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, after President Donald Trump said the war on Iran is effectively over. Stock markets climbed higher in response to the relief.

title: US Inflation Climbs 0.4% in October as Gas Prices Drop
content:
New data released after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices – shows US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October. The increase was slightly above expectations but still represents a cooldown in price increases, as the cost of gas dipped during the month.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year‑over‑year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown.
summary: US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations, as gas prices fell. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year‑over‑year CPI figure because data was not collected during the government shutdown.
author: Guardian Business

title: Senckenberg researchers uncover cold adaptation mechanisms in Antarctic spiny plunderfish
content:
With water temperatures as low as –1.9 °C (28.6 °F), the Southern Ocean is a place of extreme living conditions. A new study led by Senckenberg researchers shows how fish have adapted to Antarctic temperatures.

The researchers used the Antarctic spiny plunderfish (Harpagifer antarcticus) as a model organism and, for the first time, analyzed the maternal and paternal copies of its genome separately. This allowed them to uncover mechanisms that contribute to this group of fishes' adaptation to extreme cold.
summary: A study led by Senckenberg researchers used the Antarctic spiny plunderfish (Harpagifer antarcticus) to investigate how fish survive in the Southern Ocean's extreme cold. By separately analyzing the maternal and paternal copies of the fish's genome, the researchers uncovered mechanisms that contribute to its adaptation to temperatures as low as -1.9°C.

title: 99‑Million‑Year‑Old Feather Found in Amber Offers Clues to Flight Evolution
content: Long before birds took to the skies, dinosaurs were already sporting feathers. The precise path by which those feathers evolved into the sophisticated structures that enable flight remains unclear. A recent find—the longest feather ever preserved in amber—offers new clues to that evolutionary transition.
summary: Dinosaurs had feathers long before birds took to the skies. The longest feather ever found, a 99‑million‑year‑old feather preserved in amber, provides new clues about the evolution of flight.

content: Research from the University of Arkansas demonstrates that pure lunar regolith can be 3D‑printed into LEGO‑like bricks. Using these bricks for construction on the Moon could lessen the amount of material NASA must ship from Earth as it plans future lunar settlements.

The plan aims to enhance the resilience of indigenous and other livestock breeds, enabling them to better withstand extreme conditions across farming operations of all sizes and types.

title: Neuroscientist Baland Jalal studies sleep paralysis after personal experience
content: Neuroscientist Baland Jalal reported waking with a shadowy presence pressing on his chest, an experience that led him to investigate sleep paralysis. In his study, Jalal examines how this frightening condition may shed light on consciousness and the mind‑body connection.
summary: Neuroscientist Baland Jalal woke up feeling a shadowy presence pressing on his chest. He studied sleep paralysis to explain what the condition might reveal about consciousness.

title: Ian Sample discusses seasonal affective disorder with Oxford professor Russell Foster
content:
Ian Sample discusses the latest scientific understanding of seasonal affective disorder (SAD) with Russell Foster, professor of circadian neuroscience at the University of Oxford. The segment explores how darker days impact brain function, noting that while many people experience low mood as nights lengthen, a small proportion develop more intense depression throughout the winter months. This condition, labelled SAD since the 1980s, can be debilitating for those affected.

In the video, Foster explains the potential mechanisms behind the condition and reviews evidence regarding the most effective ways to manage it. The article also provides contact information for crisis support services, including the freephone number 116 123 for Samaritans in the UK and Ireland, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the US, and Lifeline at 13 11 14 in Australia.
summary: Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a type of depression that can become more intense during winter months, as explained by Russell Foster, professor of circadian neuroscience at the University of Oxford. The interview with Ian Sample covers the latest scientific understanding of SAD and discusses potential ways to tackle it.
author: Guardian Science

title: Experts warn GLP-1 weight‑loss focus could jeopardize insulin supply
content:
Pharma companies are increasingly prioritising GLP‑1 weight‑loss drugs, a shift that experts say could threaten the supply of insulin. The head of the Access to Medicine Foundation warned that this “gold rush” into products such as Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro may divert corporate focus from essential diabetes treatments.

GLP‑1 medications have become widespread, with Ozempic and Mounjaro gaining popularity for both obesity and diabetes management. However, many people in poorer countries still struggle to obtain basic diabetes care, including insulin.

According to a report from the Netherlands‑based non‑profit group, the industry’s attention has shifted more toward weight‑loss applications, raising concerns that insulin and other diabetes therapies could receive less emphasis.
summary: The head of the Access to Medicine Foundation says the rush into GLP‑1 weight‑loss drugs may divert attention from diabetes treatments such as insulin. The concern follows the rise of Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro, which have expanded obesity and diabetes use.

title: NASA CHAPEA Crew Exits 378-Day Isolation at Johnson Space Center
content:
The Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew exited their habitat on October 31 after completing 378 days of isolation at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. During the simulation, the team arranged photos around a boot print in simulated Martian sand outside their habitat on August 31, 2026.

Health and performance data gathered from this mission will assist NASA in developing strategies to mitigate human spaceflight risks. This research supports future Artemis and Moon Base missions.
summary: The CHAPEA Mission 2 crew exited their habitat at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston after 378 days of isolation. Health and performance data from the simulation will help NASA develop methods to counter human spaceflight risks for future Artemis and Moon Base missions.

title: NASA Studies Show LISA Can Detect Exoplanets in Binary White Dwarf Systems
content:
NASA’s latest research demonstrates that the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could identify a new class of exoplanets by detecting subtle changes in gravitational‑wave signals from binary white dwarf stars. Two papers published on Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal were led by NASA astrophysicist Casey McGrath, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. The studies show how the presence of a planet orbiting a double white dwarf system would imprint a measurable Doppler modulation on the waves emitted by the tight binary, producing sidebands at frequencies slightly above and below the primary signal.

McGrath’s first paper maps the parameter space in which LISA would be most sensitive. It identifies the planet masses and orbital periods that produce the strongest sideband signatures and estimates that a Jupiter‑mass planet could be detected in such systems out to several thousand light‑years. The second paper, coauthored with Scott Noble and Mary Anne Limbach, explores how the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) could confirm these detections. By measuring the infrared excess produced by a planet in a double white dwarf system, JWST could detect planets as small as five times the mass of Jupiter within a few hundred light‑years, while LISA would be able to find sub‑Jupiter planets under ideal circumstances.

The concept of using gravitational waves to find exoplanets was first proposed in 2008 by Japanese astronomer Naoki Seto. LISA, a joint mission led by the European Space Agency with NASA as a partner, is slated for launch in the mid‑2030s. The observatory will consist of three spacecraft trailing Earth in a triangular formation with sides of 1.6 million miles (2.5 million kilometers). Each craft carries two telescopes that transmit and receive infrared laser beams, allowing the relative distances between the spacecraft to be measured with a precision smaller than the width of a helium atom. These measurements will reveal the passing gravitational waves.

Astronomers estimate that the Milky Way contains about ten million double white dwarf systems with orbital periods of less than an hour, the frequency range that LISA is designed to probe. The mission is expected to resolve roughly ten thousand individual binaries and around one hundred mixed binaries that include white dwarfs, neutron stars, or black holes. Once LISA detects its first exoplanet candidates, the joint observations with JWST will be crucial to confirm that the gravitational‑wave sidebands correspond to real planets rather than false positives.

NASA’s contributions to LISA include the laser system, devices to control electric charge buildup on the proof masses, data‑analysis tools for source identification, and additional scientific and engineering expertise. The agency’s involvement underscores its commitment to using gravitational waves as a new tool for discovering worlds beyond our solar system.
summary: Two new studies led by NASA astrophysicists explain how the LISA observatory can identify exoplanets by detecting gravitational wave signals from tightly orbiting white dwarfs. The research also describes a method for confirming these planets using infrared observations from the James Webb Space Telescope.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Welcomes Expedition 74 Crew Home at Space Center Houston
content:
NASA will host a public event at Space Center Houston on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to welcome home the Expedition 74 crew following their return from the International Space Station. The astronauts and cosmonauts are scheduled to share mission highlights at 6 p.m. CST at the NASA Johnson Space Center’s visitor center. An awards ceremony recognizing key mission contributors will follow the presentation, and the crew members will be available for media interviews prior to the event. Media outlets may request in-person interviews by emailing the JSC Newsroom no later than 5 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 16.

The Expedition 74 team consisted of six individuals who returned to Earth in two separate groups. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev comprise the full crew. Williams, Kud-Sverchkov, and Mikaev launched aboard the Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on Nov. 27, 2025. They returned to Earth on July 26, making a parachute-assisted landing southeast of Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan. This 241-day mission, which involved 3,856 orbits and traveled more than 102 million miles, was the first for Williams and Mikaev and the second for Kud-Sverchkov.

Meir, Hathaway, and Adenot launched aboard a Dragon spacecraft on Feb. 13 as part of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. After more than seven months in orbit, the trio splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles on Oct. 8. Their 237-day mission included more than 3,792 orbits and traveled over 100 million miles. This was the second mission for Meir and the first for Hathaway and Adenot. Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev also flew as part of Crew-12 but is unavailable for the upcoming event.

During their time in space, the Expedition 74 crew dedicated more than 1,400 hours to scientific research and technology demonstrations. Their work advanced in-space manufacturing by testing metal and tissue 3D-printing technologies and supported human health studies examining the effects of long-duration spaceflight. Specific research included blood flow studies, assessments of piloting capabilities under changing gravitational conditions, and the activation of a new compact exercise system. The crew also evaluated life-support and environmental systems critical to future exploration missions under NASA’s Artemis program.

Additional scientific efforts included pharmaceutical research to crystalize proteins for cancer medications, advance tumor targeting treatments, and grow stem cells for therapeutics. The crew cared for the first set of plants studied outside of curated systems and upgraded an instrument used to advance the understanding of matter and develop new quantum technologies. They also managed visiting spacecraft and performed essential maintenance to support the continued operation of the orbiting laboratory. Beyond research, the crew engaged students and audiences globally through live educational events, outreach activities, and the sharing of imagery highlighting international collaboration in space.
summary: (March 15, 2026) — The International Space Station orbits 267 miles above a cloudy Atlantic Ocean southwest of Cape Town, South Africa. The Kibo laboratory module’s External Platform and the Canadarm2 robotic arm highlight the top foreground above Earth’s terminator—the line between night and day—in this photograph taken at approximately 6:36 a.

title: Chrome ships Modern Web Guidance 1.0 to help coding agents use native web primitives
content: Browsers natively handle a lot of what used to take 50 lines of JS (or a dependency): `CSS. Highlights` for text range highlighting without s everywhere, ` ` and showModal() give you backdrops and ideal focus management, `field-sizing` to auto-grow textareas as the user types.. (Something yesterday's ftrain post touched on [0]) Models know about some of these by name, but consistently won't default to using the platform-native solution and instead prefer the incumbent +JS based pattern. We started an effort in Chrome to supplement coding agents with this key domain knowledge and we're shipping our 1.0 today, in collaboration with Firefox, MDN, and Edge. 200+ guides (~1.7MB) of curated, hand-crafted implementation best-practices from web experts, updated as the web evolves. (Open source, obv, so.. We'll welcome your bikeshedding ;) Readable versions here: [1] I've spent the last 9 months obsessing over how to ship this as an agent skill + (Agentic RAG) CLI without blowing up your context window. (Or cedeing activation mechanics to MCP dynamic tool search). The skill description is minmaxed for activating on relevant frontend tasks. The RAG work I'm pretty proud of… originally a 500mb native stack down to a ~7MB pure-JS package, ~10ms search on your CPU. We just introduced a deterministic 'legacy-scan' (trained on 30k github repos) to identify old 'n dusted patterns that your agent can modernize. (92% avg precision on held-out repos.) People make a lot of claims about what coding agents are good/bad at. We wanted receipts, so we invested heavily in eval infra [2] to help us hill-climb, but also to identify when knowledge is common enough we can prune our guides. (Ofc, some of the things we thought AI didn't know turned out to be wrong :) We run codex/claude/agy against 200 tasks without the skill and then with.. In total ~1,700 playwright/AST-based assertions. Agents go from 55% pass unguided to 92% guided. Try it out: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest install DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate dialog modal" DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan./src If you spot something wrong or weird, give us a holler! Longer write-up on the 1.0: https://developer. Chrome. Com/blog/modern-web-guidance-v1 --- 0: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50416456 1: https://developer. Chrome. Com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides 2: https://googlechrome. Github. Io/modern-web-guidance-src/ Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50443812 Points: 9 # Comments: 1
summary: Chrome ships Modern Web Guidance 1.0 to help coding agents use native web primitives.

title: Outokumpu’s EvoMaterials platform aims to rethink metal extraction
content:
The metals industry has long been shaped by landmark innovations such as the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting. Despite these breakthroughs, most extraction methods still rely on scientific foundations that have remained largely unchanged for more than a century. Outokumpu, the global leader in sustainable stainless steel and ferrochrome production, is questioning this status quo through its EvoMaterials platform, a technology initiative aimed at rethinking how metals are extracted.

The need for new approaches is driven by a growing demand for critical metals. As economies expand and electrification spreads, data and scientific models show that minerals are required for data centers, aerospace, water treatment, energy systems, and defence. At the same time, many Western economies have reduced domestic processing capacity for the very metals that these industries depend on. Metallurgy is therefore becoming strategically important, with considerations of cost, availability, carbon footprint, geographic origin, and supply‑chain resilience shaping the sector. This is especially true for chromium and other specialty metals used in high‑temperature and extreme‑environment applications.

EvoMaterials originated from research into sulfidation‑based processing technologies, initially pursued to lower the carbon emissions associated with ferrochrome production. Laboratory work revealed that these alternative chemistries could recover valuable metals from lower‑grade resources and industrial side streams while fundamentally altering separation processes. The platform aims to rethink mineral resource use, increase resource efficiency, and strengthen industrial competitiveness.

The technology began in the United States in 2021, processing chromite from Outokumpu’s Kemi mine in Finland—the only chrome mine in the European Union and one of the few such operations in the Western world. Since then, Outokumpu has refined the process through extensive research and development, combining new chemistries with proprietary metallurgical expertise and a non‑exclusive patent license agreement from MIT. The new method creates a different chemical environment that enables more efficient extraction with fewer losses and by‑products, allowing recovery of critical materials from resources previously considered waste.

EvoMaterials is described as a technology platform rather than a single process. Once a new extraction pathway is mastered for one material system, the same scientific principles may be adapted to other metals and mineral resources. The next step is pilot‑scale validation: a plant in New Hampshire will begin operations in the first half of 2027, scaling the technology from laboratory to one‑ton production. The goal is industrial‑scale deployment by 2030, with the potential to produce low‑CO₂ chromium‑enriched ferrochrome and chromium metal, and to adapt the platform to nickel, molybdenum, and other strategic materials. The initiative raises a broader question about whether today’s metallurgical processes could look different if invented from scratch, suggesting that the next revolution in materials may begin by rethinking metal extraction itself.
summary: Outokumpu has developed EvoMaterials, a technology platform that uses sulfidation-based processing to extract metals more efficiently and produce low‑CO2 ferrochrome and chromium metal. A pilot plant in New Hampshire will begin operations in the first half of 2027 to validate the technology.

title: Scott Wiener, Pelosi’s successor, plans to regulate AI amid data center power concerns
content: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI —Grace Huckins As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy. I spoke with Wiener only a few hours after he had been declared the victor. But he was already thinking about AI risk: during our 20-minute conversation, he used the phrase “recursive self-improvement” half a dozen times. “We need to slow this down,” he told me. “Because it’s moving very quickly, and we could sleepwalk into a disaster.” Still, he describes himself as only “cautiously optimistic” about Congress’s ability to rein in AI. Here’s what he plans to do about it. The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity —James O’Donnell As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash sweeping the country arguably first began to take shape. Big Tech has framed the data center uproar as a culture war over progress. But a few days in Ashburn convinced me the real fault line may be electricity: drawing it from the grid or generating it onsite provokes different forms of blowback. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity. Find out why. This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. One More Thing China wants to restore the sea with high-tech marine ranches Just a short ferry ride from the Chinese port city of Yantai sits Genghai No. 1, a strange offshore complex that combines a tourist attraction with an industrial fish farm. title: eBay blocks Meta's Muse AI agent from browsing platform
content:
eBay has reportedly blocked AI agents from browsing the site, including Meta’s Muse, marking a new obstacle in the AI‑agent race. A reader told The Verge that for several weeks Muse had been able to browse eBay, curate a daily digest of watches for sale, and provide links, prices, shipping details and notes on condition or style.

This weekend Muse was unable to pull any links or details from eBay, reporting that it was blocked from the platform. The Verge was able to re‑create the experience using other search requests, and in some cases found that Muse instead directed users elsewhere.
summary: eBay has blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from browsing the site, preventing it from pulling links or details about listings. The Verge was able to recreate the experience using other search requests and found that Muse directed users elsewhere in some cases.
author: The Verge

title: Anthropic unveils AI office suite with Claude Meetings, Sheets, and W
content:
Anthropic unveiled a new AI-powered suite of office tools at a San Francisco event on Tuesday, aiming to expand its reach beyond enterprise and coding clients to other knowledge workers. The company, which previously inspired competitors like OpenAI, SpaceXSI, and Meta, is targeting non-technical professionals who spend significant time attending meetings, brainstorming, and analyzing metrics.

The announcement follows an earlier hype cycle for Claude Code and marks a strategic shift toward broader productivity applications. The new offerings include Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets, and Claude W, designed specifically to assist users in these common business tasks.
summary: Anthropic launched a new suite of AI-powered office tools for non-technical workers at an event in San Francisco. The new products, including Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets, and Claude W, are designed to assist with meetings, brainstorming, and metrics analysis.
author: The Verge

title: Google Fi is bringing back multiple cell network support for better coverage
content:
Google Fi is launching a new “super network” feature that automatically switches users between two different 5G networks to improve connectivity. The update begins rolling out today on Pixel 9 and newer devices where Google Fi is active on eSIM and any non-Fi SIMs are disabled. Jane Harnett, Google Fi Wireless senior product manager, spoke to The Verge regarding the feature’s return.

This capability marks a revival of multi-network support for the service. When Google Fi launched in 2015, users could switch between T-Mobile and Sprint networks. That functionality ceased after T-Mobile acquired Sprint in 2020, merging the two networks into one.
summary: Google Fi is launching a new "super network" that can automatically switch users between two different 5G networks depending on which one has better connectivity. The feature is rolling out starting today on Pixel 9 and newer phones that have Google Fi active on eSIM and have any non-Fi SIMs disabled.
author: The Verge

title: IGF jurors vow to reject AI games after Big Walk dev admits limited AI use
content:
Some Independent Games Festival (IGF) jurors issued a statement declaring they would not vote for games using generative AI in any capacity. The jurors noted a significant increase in entries developed with these tools, which sparked intense discussion and disagreement without reaching a universal consensus, despite describing this year’s submissions as incredible.

In response, the developer of the indie hit Big Walk stated that AI was used sparingly during the final stretch of development to help resolve difficult technical challenges and bugs.
summary: Independent Games Festival jurors stated they will not vote for games using generative AI in any capacity. The developer of Big Walk confirmed they used AI sparingly during the final stretch of development to address technical challenges and bugs.
author: The Verge

title: Ableton Live 13 announced with step sequencer, new drum synth
content:
Ableton announced Live 13 today, with a release window set for early 2027. The update brings a range of new features, making it the biggest change to the digital audio workstation in years.

A standout addition is a proper step sequencer, which had previously existed only on the Push controller or via the piano roll. The desktop app now lets users adjust velocity, timing, chance, length, and repeats for each step.

The release also includes a new drum synthesizer and other enhancements, though further details are not yet disclosed.
summary: Ableton announced Live 13, expected to arrive in early 2027, featuring a new step sequencer, drum synth, and other updates. The new step sequencer allows users to change velocity, timing, chance, length, and repeats for each step.
author: The Verge

title: ChatGPT Launches Verified Business Agents for US E-commerce
content:
OpenAI is introducing verified “Business Agents” to ChatGPT, enabling users to interact with brand representatives for tasks such as comparison shopping. This feature launches in beta as part of a new suite of business-focused tools and is initially available to eligible e-commerce and online service companies in the United States.

Users can initiate conversations with a Business Agent when a participating company appears in a ChatGPT response. During these interactions, individuals may inquire about specific offerings and ask follow-up questions, such as comparing differences between two products. Businesses retain control over the agent’s behavior by specifying particular parameters for their digital representation.
summary: OpenAI is introducing verified Business Agents in ChatGPT that allow users to chat with brand representatives for tasks like comparison shopping. The feature is launching in beta for eligible e-commerce and online service businesses in the US.
author: The Verge

title: Ukraine's fiber-optic drones face supply squeeze as AI data centers demand fiber
content:
Fiber-optic drones, which are immune to battlefield jamming due to their physical cable connection to operators, have become a prevalent weapon in the war in Ukraine. The widespread use of these drones has left fields and forests scattered with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. However, importing the necessary fiber-optic material from China has become increasingly expensive as demand from global AI data centers competes with military needs for the same limited supply.

The use of unjammable fiber-optic drones originated with the Russian military, which deployed them in 2024 to repel Ukrainian forces during the cross-border incursion into the Kursk Oblast. Ukrainian forces subsequently adopted similar technology to counter electronic warfare jamming that typically neutralizes radio-controlled drones. Since the start of the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022, Ukraine has continuously developed various drone innovations, including first-person view quadcopters and heavier models.

Both Russia and Ukraine have relied on Chinese suppliers for off-the-shelf drones and components, including bulk fiber-optic cable. Finished spools of this cable allow drones to operate at ranges of dozens of miles, with extreme cases reaching up to 62 miles (100 kilometers), according to the independent Russian publication The Insider. Facing rising costs and supply constraints, Ukrainian drone makers are now adapting their production methods.
summary: Ukraine's fiber-optic drones face supply squeeze as AI data centers demand fiber.
author: Ars Technica

title: Polestar Debuts Formula 2030 Concept With Low Roofline and Saab‑Inspired Design
content:
Polestar unveiled its Formula 2030 concept today, a new electric car that builds on the brand’s heritage as a former Volvo racing team. The automaker, now a spin‑off of Volvo and backed by Geely, has developed the concept as a styling exercise that sits between the upcoming Polestar 2 and the larger Polestar 7. Polestar notes that the model’s numbering follows a chronological scheme rather than size.

The Formula 2030 shares the same length as the Polestar 2 but features a very low roofline, giving it a two‑box silhouette reminiscent of Saab’s Aero‑X concept from 2008. The design also incorporates rear lights that the company says will appear on future production Polestars.

Polestar has not confirmed whether the hatchback layout will move into series production. The concept is currently only a design study, and Polestars remain unavailable in the United States due to the Chinese ownership of Geely and related congressional restrictions.
summary: Perhaps only a small percentage of Ars readers will care about the Polestar 2030 concept, debuted today by the electric automaker. Spun out of Volvo—once upon a time, Polestar was a racing team—the brand has leveraged the resources of parent-automaker Geely to create electric vehicles that marry a modern minimalist style with rewarding driving dynamics.
author: Ars Technica

title: FDA warns GLP-1 drugs may pose risk of rare eye condition causing vision loss
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a drug safety communication warning that several popular obesity medications may carry a “potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition that can cause permanent vision loss. The drugs named in the warning include Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound and Mounjaro.  

The FDA’s alert focuses on non‑arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a condition caused by restricted blood flow to the optic nerve. NAION can lead to swelling, cell death and damage to the nerve, resulting in abrupt and often permanent vision loss. The agency notes that it is unknown how GLP‑1 receptor agonists might trigger NAION.  

NAION is rare, occurring in roughly 2 to 10 people per 100,000 in the general population, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology. Because many risk factors for NAION—such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, metabolic syndrome and obstructive sleep apnea—are common among patients who take GLP‑1 drugs, establishing a definitive link has been difficult. The FDA now requires manufacturers of GLP‑1 receptor agonists to add a warning about this risk to their drug labels.
summary: FDA has warned that GLP‑1 receptor agonist drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, and Mounjaro may increase the risk of non‑arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a rare eye condition that can cause permanent vision loss. The agency will require manufacturers to add a warning about this risk to their drug labels.
author: Ars Technica

title: Nvidia Board Investigation Threatens Jensen Huang's Future as CEO
content:
Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang, putting the future of the company’s longest‑serving executive at risk. Huang, who co‑founded the chipmaker more than 30 years ago, has admitted to an extramarital affair with an executive at a large Nvidia customer. U.S. officials also allege that the customer executive was working as a Chinese spy, adding to the scrutiny.

The investigation threatens to force Huang out of the CEO role at the world’s second‑most‑valuable company, a prospect that has alarmed investors and allies in the tech industry. Nvidia’s shares fell more than 5 percent by midday on Monday, following a broader sell‑off in AI stocks that saw the company lose its position as the world’s most valuable firm to Apple late last month.
summary: An investigation by Nvidia’s board into Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair threatens his position as chief executive. Shares fell more than 5% after the news, amid concerns that he could be forced out.
author: Ars Technica

title: DeepMind unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark ASIMOV-jailbreak
content: Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. DeepMind's physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There's the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that's Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5. DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. Read full article Comments
summary: Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do.
author: Ars Technica

title: Axiom Space sues Vast Space over alleged copying of proprietary NASA document
content:
A lawsuit has been filed in federal court by Houston‑based Axiom Space against Long Beach, California‑based Vast Space, alleging that Vast used Axiom’s proprietary information in a mission‑planning document submitted to NASA. According to court filings unsealed by a November 4 order from U.S. District Judge Charles Eskridge, Axiom is pursuing a False Claims Act case, claiming that Vast presented NASA with a fraudulent document that incorporated Axiom’s confidential material.

The dispute arises amid NASA’s competition to develop private space stations slated for launch in the 2030s. Companies participating in the program must submit final proposals to the agency by December 14, a deadline that is now less than a month away. The lawsuit adds a legal dimension to the already intense race among the leading contenders.
summary: NASA's competition for the development of private space stations that will take flight in the 2030s is already nearing crunch time. But a recently unsealed lawsuit may spice things up even further.
author: Ars Technica

title: Fossil fuel emissions dip 0.4% in 2026 amid Iran war and high oil prices
content:
A new analysis indicates that global fossil‑fuel carbon emissions fell by roughly 0.4 percent in 2026 compared with the previous year. The study was led by Corinne Le Quéré of the University of East Anglia. Researchers attribute the decline to a short‑term dip caused by the war in Iran and the resulting rise in oil prices, rather than to a lasting shift in climate‑policy progress.

While annual greenhouse‑gas emissions have generally risen steadily, the analysts note that various factors can occasionally pull a year off the long‑term trend. They view the 2026 reduction as an anomaly linked to the temporary economic impact of higher oil costs, not a permanent reversal of the upward emissions trajectory.
summary: A new analysis led by Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia estimates fossil fuel emissions fell about 0.4 percent in 2026 from the previous year. Researchers say the short‑term decline is driven by the war in Iran and its effect on oil prices.
author: Ars Technica

title: Valve shares Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED frame‑rate data on Store pages
content:
Valve has begun publishing anonymized frame‑rate data for a growing number of Steam Store titles, showing average performance and histograms for both the Steam Deck and the Steam Deck OLED. The data, which has been collected from Steam users who opted in since February, is now displayed on many store pages to give players a clearer picture of how games run on the handheld.

The company notes that enabling VSync or setting frame‑rate limits can skew the collected figures and that the statistics do not reflect any custom in‑game settings that users might apply. Despite these caveats, Valve reports that the frame‑rate numbers tend to cluster within relatively narrow ranges. This move follows the 2021 launch of the Steam Deck Verified program, which some players felt did not always correspond to actual game performance on the device.
summary: Valve shares Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED frame‑rate data on Store pages.
author: Ars Technica

title: N-able takes access service offline after researcher publishes dozens of zero‑day bugs
content: N-able has taken its remote access service offline following the publication of dozens of zero‑day vulnerabilities by a researcher. The company also advised its self‑hosted customers to shut down their own servers, describing the situation as a “critical security incident” and warning of potential cyberattacks.
summary: N-able took its access service offline after a researcher published dozens of zero‑day bugs. The company also urged self‑hosted customers to shut down their servers because of a critical security incident and the risk of cyberattacks.
author: TechCrunch

title: Sundrop iPhone app creates baby photo recaps and time‑lapses using on‑device AI
content: Sundrop, a new iPhone app, employs Apple’s on‑device AI to let parents sift through their baby photo collections and generate recaps, time‑lapse videos and other keepsakes, all while keeping images stored locally and avoiding cloud uploads.
summary: Sundrop is a new iPhone app that turns baby photos into recaps, time‑lapses and other keepsakes. It uses Apple’s on‑device AI to let parents rediscover photos without uploading them to the cloud.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to convert workplace talks into plans and tasks
content: Anthropic has introduced Claude Meetings, a tool designed to convert workplace discussions into actionable plans and tasks. During conversations, Claude can draft the discussed plan, create a timeline on a whiteboard, respond to questions in the meeting chat, and pull data from linked work apps, such as last year’s figures.
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings, a tool that turns workplace discussions into plans and tasks. Claude can draft the discussed plan, map a timeline on a whiteboard, answer meeting‑chat questions, and retrieve information from connected work apps such as last year's figures.
author: TechCrunch

title: Martin Scorsese partners with AI firm to use text‑to‑image model for storyboards
content: As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids. That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm, citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon ; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”. The current canary in the coalmine however is the storyboard artist, whose work gen AI appears to have directly in its sights. Storyboard artists are the illustrators who draw the panels of images with notes and diagrams that map out scenes before they are filmed. Storyboards are used to work out how a film will look, and as a blueprint to communicate a director’s vision to cast and crew, and are one of the first steps in bringing a script off the page. Now they appear on the verge of replacement by programmes that use text prompts to create illustrations instead. Even an old-school diehard like Martin Scorsese has got on board; in June he announced a partnership with an AI firm whose text-to-image model he used in the storyboarding process for his next movie.
summary: In June, Martin Scorsese announced a partnership with an AI firm and used its text‑to‑image model to create storyboards for his next film. The adoption mirrors a broader Hollywood trend, with directors like James Cameron, Steven Soderbergh and Christopher Nolan also experimenting with generative AI, prompting concerns for storyboard artists.
author: Guardian Technology

title: OpenAI's Teen Mode enrolls all users under 18, raising concerns about teen mental health
content:
OpenAI introduced “Teen Mode” for ChatGPT in August, automatically enrolling every user under 18 in the new version of the service. The rollout follows a lawsuit that alleged the chatbot contributed to the suicide of a 16‑year‑old, Adam Raine, filed a year earlier.  

The article notes that critics argue the change could affect young students beyond cognitive skills, potentially undermining a reliable sense of their own minds. It also observes that the tech industry has repeatedly contested causal links in similar lawsuits that claim companies designed products to exploit children.
summary: In August, OpenAI launched Teen Mode, automatically enrolling every user under 18. The launch follows a lawsuit alleging ChatGPT contributed to the suicide of 16‑year‑old Adam Raine and ongoing industry disputes over product harms to children.
author: Guardian Technology

title: XPeng says two‑seat flying car could be available in China next summer
content:
XPeng announced that its two‑seat, low‑altitude vehicle could be available for trips in China as early as next summer. Chief executive Deli Zhao said the $300,000 device will be ready for recreational users in rural locations and for emergency‑service operations in the second half of 2027.

The model, which incorporates autopilot technology, follows a decade of development that included flying‑motorbike trials at the company’s Guangzhou base. China’s civil aviation authorities have approved the vehicle for limited use.
summary: XPeng announced its $300,000 low‑altitude two‑seat flying car could be ready for recreational use in rural China as early as next summer. Chief executive Deli Zhao said the vehicle will also be available to emergency services in the second half of 2027 after approval for limited use by China’s civil aviation authorities.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic aims for up to $1.4tn valuation in upcoming stock market flotation
content:
Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, is seeking a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion (£1.05 trillion) in its imminent stock‑market flotation, according to a U.S. regulatory filing released on Tuesday. The figure is lower than earlier reports that had suggested the company was targeting a $2 trillion initial public offering on Wall Street.

The reduction follows a period in which investors cooled on artificial‑intelligence investments and began questioning the durability of the AI boom, prompting the company to adjust its valuation expectations.
summary: Anthropic aims for up to $1.4tn valuation in upcoming stock market flotation.
author: Guardian Technology

title: UK under‑16 social media ban may extend to YouTube Kids and 150 platforms
content:
Sources briefed on the government’s proposals indicate that regulations for a social media ban for under-16s could expand to cover up to 150 platforms. This substantial extension might inadvertently include sites previously thought to be exempt, such as YouTube Kids, as well as games platforms like Lego Play. Other services potentially affected by the new rules include Spotify and eBay.

The expanded regulations are currently under consideration and are set to come into force in March. One source close to the talks confirmed that the scope of the ban now includes these additional digital services, marking a significant broadening of the initial legislative target.
summary: Regulations being considered could expand the UK ban on social media for under‑16s to include YouTube Kids and other sites previously thought exempt. The proposals could cover up to 150 platforms such as LegoPlay, Spotify and eBay, with the ban slated to start in March.
author: Guardian Technology

title: MWC26 in Doha highlights MENA mobile economy to hit €421bn while millions stay offline
content: MWC26 returned to Doha, where officials noted that the mobile economy in the Middle East and North Africa is projected to reach €421 billion. At the same time, the industry highlighted a dual challenge: constructing networks capable of supporting artificial intelligence while closing a digital divide that leaves millions of people without mobile internet access.
summary: MWC26 returned to Doha and projected the mobile economy in MENA to reach €421 billion. The event highlighted a dual challenge of building networks for artificial intelligence and narrowing a digital divide that leaves millions without mobile internet.
author: Euronews

title: Drone footage shows devastation after deadly Yambol highway pile‑up killing 11
content: Drone footage captured the aftermath of a massive pile‑up on a fog‑shrouded highway near Yambol, Bulgaria, showing dozens of vehicles involved. State media reported that the crash killed 11 people and left dozens more injured.
summary: Drone footage shows the aftermath of a massive pile‑up involving dozens of vehicles on a foggy highway near Yambol, Bulgaria. State media reported that 11 people were killed and dozens injured.
author: Euronews

title: Qatar says progress in US-Iran talks after PM meets Trump
content: A day after Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met President Trump at the White House, a Qatari foreign‑ministry spokesman said both parties were issuing positive statements about a diplomatic solution to the U.S.–Iran issue. He added that Qatar cannot assess how close or how far an agreement may be.
summary: Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met President Trump at the White House. A Qatari foreign ministry spokesman said both sides were making positive statements about a diplomatic solution but could not say how close an agreement is.
author: Euronews

title: Prince Harry and Meghan visit EU Parliament in Brussels for child‑online safety event
content: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan visited the European Parliament in Brussels on Tuesday, 10 November, to discuss the dangers children face online. During the visit they met families affected by online abuse, after which Harry addressed the gathering.
summary: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan visited the European Parliament in Brussels on Tuesday 10 November to discuss the dangers children face online. They met families affected by online abuse before Harry addressed the gathering.
author: Euronews

title: Russia applies unfriendly countries list to child custody, vehicle registration, debts
content: Moscow’s list of states it deems unfriendly was set in March 2022 for foreign economic policy, but decrees and court rulings now apply it to child custody, vehicle registration and debt repayment.
summary: Moscow’s list of states it deems unfriendly was set in March 2022 for foreign economic policy. Decrees and court rulings now apply it to child custody, vehicle registration and debt repayment.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV visits Argentina in second leg of South American tour
content: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina for the second leg of his South American tour, following a stop in Uruguay. While in Argentina he celebrated public Masses, met the faithful and held talks with religious and government leaders. The pontiff’s tour will conclude in Peru.
summary: Pope Leo XIV visited Argentina on the second leg of his South American tour after a stop in Uruguay. He celebrated public Masses, met the faithful and held talks with religious and government leaders, with Peru as the tour’s final stop.
author: France 24

title: French students pledge continued protests for better learning conditions
content: France’s street protests, which began in September, were initially led by students demanding renovation of school buildings, an increase in teachers, and university reforms. The movement later expanded into broader cost‑of‑living protests, drawing in trade unions and political activists, and at times turning violent.
summary: French students joined protests that began in September demanding school renovations, more teachers and university reforms. The demonstrations have broadened into cost‑of‑living protests with trade unions and political activists and have sometimes turned violent.
author: France 24

title: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth dismisses impeachment bid as political spectacle
content: U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth called the impeachment effort against him “a political spectacle” on Tuesday, a day after Republican Representative Thomas Massie announced a bid to impeach him over Hegseth’s handling of the war in Iran and other actions. The article notes that Hegseth is a former Fox News host and a military veteran, and that he has risen to become one of the most prominent figures in the Trump administration.
summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "political spectacle". Republican Thomas Massie launched the bid over Hegseth's handling of the unpopular war in Iran and other actions; Hegseth is a former Fox News host and military veteran who has become a prominent figure in the Trump administration.
author: France 24

title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth calls impeachment effort a farce
content:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday, November 10, that an effort to impeach him over abuse of power in the Iran war is a farce and sabotage that plays into the hands of adversaries.  

FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.
summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday, November 10 that the effort to impeach him over abuse of power in the Iran war is a farce. He also said the attempt is sabotage that plays into the hands of adversaries.
author: France 24

title: Kristallnacht' 88th anniversary: Merz says Germany faces historic test over antisemitism
content: It has been 88 years since "Kristallnacht", the "Night of Broken Glass" in Europe, a violent pogrom against the Jewish population across Nazi Germany and Austria, marking a critical escalation toward the Holocaust. Friedrich Merz, Federal Chancellor of Germany, said that Germany currently faces a historic test over antisemitism.
summary: It has been 88 years since "Kristallnacht", the "Night of Broken Glass" in Europe, a violent pogrom against the Jewish population across Nazi Germany and Austria, marking a critical escalation toward the Holocaust. Friedrich Merz, Federal Chancellor of Germany, said that Germany currently faces a historic test over antisemitism.
author: France 24

title: Teddy Riner reportedly announces 2027 French presidential bid, echoing sports stars
content: French judo champion Teddy Riner reportedly announced on Monday a bid for the 2027 French presidential election. The piece notes that he joins other sports figures who have moved from athletic arenas to political platforms, and suggests readers explore several notable predecessors.
summary: French judo star Teddy Riner may have announced his bid for the 2027 French presidential campaign on Monday. He joins other sports figures who have moved from athletics to political roles.
author: France 24

title: French police search Ritz hotel and Al Fayed properties in women‑trafficking probe
content:
French police searched several properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, as part of a probe into a suspected international network trafficking women for Mohamed Al Fayed. Prosecutors told AFP on Tuesday.

The Ritz is one of the late tycoon's high‑end ventures where victims have said they faced abuse.
summary: French police searched several properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, in an investigation into a suspected international network trafficking women for Mohamed Al Fayed, prosecutors said. The Ritz is one of the late tycoon's high‑end ventures where victims have said they faced abuse.
author: France 24

title: Filming amongst body bags: New Colombian president’s comms campaign sparks backlash
content:
Since assuming the presidency in August, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has posted a series of videos that showcase his security forces and their operations against armed groups. In several clips the president is seen speaking while standing among body bags; other footage includes prisoners or resembles scenes from an action film.

The visual campaign has prompted a growing outcry, with critics condemning the president’s social‑media posts as glorifying repressive policies.
summary: Since taking office in August, new far-right Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella has shared video after video promoting his security forces – especially operations they’ve carried out against armed groups. In some, De la Espriella speaks standing among body bags.
author: France 24

title: Thick fog causes Bulgaria highway pileup, killing 12 and injuring dozens
content: A series of highway crashes in Bulgaria, attributed to thick fog, left at least 12 people dead and dozens injured. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene to conduct rescue operations.
summary: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.
author: DW World

title: Japan watches for shift in Trump's foreign policy after midterm loss
content: Tokyo is monitoring whether President Donald Trump’s foreign‑policy focus will shift after the “drubbing” he suffered in last week’s U.S. midterm election. Japanese officials fear the loss could prompt Trump to chase a diplomatic quick win that might come at the expense of Washington’s Indo‑Pacific allies.
summary: Tokyo fears the drubbing US President Donald Trump suffered in last week's midterm election may push him to pursue a diplomatic quick win. Japan worries this could come at the expense of Washington's allies in the Indo‑Pacific.
author: DW World

title: New exhibition explores links between colonialism and Nazism, prompting debate
content: Hitler once referred to Eastern Europe as “Germany’s India.” A new exhibition now explores connections between colonialism and Nazism, presenting the ongoing, contentious debate over how such comparisons help or hinder historical understanding.
summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and a bitter debate surrounds where such comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.
author: DW World

title: Iran denies involvement in supermarket fridge hack as France summons ambassador
content:
France said it rules “nothing” out after a cyberattack targeted supermarket refrigeration units and summoned Iran’s ambassador in response.  

Iran categorically rejected Paris’ accusations, describing them as “baseless and one‑sided” and denying any involvement of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
summary: France said it is leaving all possibilities open after a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units and summoned Iran’s ambassador. Iran categorically rejected the accusations, calling them baseless and one‑sided and denying IRGC involvement.
author: DW World

title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
content: Polish victims of the Nazi regime, more than 80 years after World War II, say they are still awaiting a “humanitarian gesture” from Germany. They note that the draft budget for 2027 offers little hope for any reparations.
summary: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.
author: DW World

title: Slovak PM accuses Friedrich Merz of blackmail over Ukraine aid demand in EU budget
content:
Friedrich Merz has signaled that he will block the EU’s seven‑year budget unless a financial aid deal for Ukraine is reached. The German chancellor has also warned that the burden of the budget is carried mostly by a few member states.  

The Slovak prime minister and other European leaders have accused Merz of “typical blackmail” over the Ukraine aid issue. Their criticism has angered central‑European leaders who are net beneficiaries of EU funds but do not want to participate in the upcoming funding round for Ukraine’s war effort.  

These developments are expected to set the stage for stormy talks later this month.
summary: Friedrich Merz said he will block the EU’s seven‑year budget unless a deal on financial aid for Ukraine is reached. The Slovak prime minister accused Merz of blackmail, and other central European leaders expressed anger at the stance.

title: US officials aim for final end to Russia-Ukraine war as Abu Dhabi talks continue
content:
U.S. officials said they are pursuing a “final end” to the Russia‑Ukraine war as trilateral peace talks began in Abu Dhabi. The negotiations, described as the first substantive talks between the two sides since February, include a U.S. proposal for a “long‑term security architecture” linking Moscow and Europe.

The talks are scheduled to continue into a second day on Wednesday. They also mark the first such dialogue since the United States carried out joint strikes with Israel against Iran and follow recent U.S. midterm elections that have reduced Donald Trump’s domestic standing.
summary: US officials aim for final end to Russia-Ukraine war as Abu Dhabi talks continue.

title: UK launches 10‑nation maritime defence pact after 41% rise in Russian naval activity
content: New alliance with the Netherlands and Baltic and Nordic countries comes in response to 41% increase in Russian naval activity around UK Russian naval activity around the UK has increased by 41% in the first nine months of the year, a British defence minister has said, as the Royal Navy announced plans to step up a 10-country maritime defensive effort in response. Luke Pollard, the minister for defence readiness, described the figure as “a huge increase”, justifying a new drone and warship initiative from “the alliance of beer-drinking nations” – the UK, the Netherlands and the Baltic and Nordic countries.
summary: Russian naval activity around the UK increased by 41% in the first nine months of the year, according to Luke Pollard, the minister for defence readiness. The Royal Navy announced a 10‑country maritime defensive effort involving the UK, the Netherlands and Baltic and Nordic countries, with a new drone and warship initiative.

title: Britain open to paying EU for electricity market access, says minister Hamish Falconer
content:
Britain is prepared to discuss payments to the European Union in exchange for access to the EU electricity market, cabinet minister Hamish Falconer said.  Falconer, who is leading the UK’s renegotiation of its bilateral relationship with the EU, noted that the United Kingdom has not accepted the principle of linking electricity trade to the EU’s cohesion fund.  Instead, he said the UK is willing to consider contributing to infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU.

The minister told the Guardian that the UK and EU will discuss the matter after this month’s summit, as ministers look to deepen ties with the union over the next few years.
summary: Britain open to paying EU for electricity market access, says minister Hamish Falconer.

title: Greens warn Labor’s refusal to preference minor party in Prahran risks Liberal‑One Nation coalition
content:
The Victorian Greens have warned that the Labor Party’s choice not to give preferences to a minor progressive party in the inner‑city seat of Prahran could enable a Liberal‑One Nation coalition to win the upcoming election. Party leader Ellen Sandell described the move as “frankly unforgivable” and said it risks handing power to the right‑wing alliance.

Sandell’s criticism followed Labor’s decision on Tuesday to run an open ticket in Prahran, a Melbourne electorate currently held by Liberal MP Rachel Westaway, who holds the seat with a 1.3 percent margin. The Greens argue that the lack of preferences may shift the balance in the closely contested race.
summary: Ellen Sandell, leader of the Victorian Greens, called Labor’s decision not to preference a minor party in Prahran “frankly unforgivable”. She said the open ticket in the inner‑Melbourne seat held by Liberal Rachel Westaway with a 1.3% margin could hand power to a Liberal‑One Nation coalition.

title: John Kerry says US and others must follow China's green energy lead
content: Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’ Cop31 live – latest updates China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit. As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
summary: John Kerry says US and others must follow China's green energy lead.

title: UK and Argentina dispute Falklands Sea Lion oil project as Hamburg ITLOS hearing begins
content:
The Sea Lion oil project in the North Falkland basin has prompted Argentina to tell an international tribunal that Britain’s approval of drilling off the Falkland Islands has dramatically deepened a sovereignty dispute that led to war four decades ago.  

At the opening of a historic legal clash before the Hamburg‑based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS), an Argentinian legal team argued that the oil project should be suspended.
summary: Argentina told the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea in Hamburg that Britain's approval of the Sea Lion oil drilling project in the North Falkland basin has deepened the sovereignty dispute over the Falkland Islands. An Argentine legal team argued at the start of the ITLOS hearing that the project should be suspended.

title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid warehouses
content:
Lewis Hamilton, a seven‑time Formula One world champion, visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip. During the trip he toured the border area and logistics warehouses operated by the Egyptian Red Crescent and met organisations that are sending humanitarian aid into Gaza.

The champion has previously spoken out about the conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, calling for peace. He has also used social media to highlight children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and to call for a ceasefire.

title: Review: Musical 'Wanted' at James Earl Jones Theatre lacks grit
content:
The musical Wanted is currently running at the James Earl Jones theatre in New York City. The production, written by Angelica Chéri and composed by Ross Baum, presents a “mostly true” tale about two 19th-century sisters evading law enforcement. The story is based on the lives of Chéri’s great-great aunts, Mary and Martha Clarke, who were daughters of an emancipated sharecropper. The sisters, described as light-skinned, attempt to pass in the white world to earn money for their mother, Tallulah, with the goal of purchasing the cotton-field land she had worked for decades.

The show opens with a high-volume, portentous musical tone and a Greek chorus dressed in billowing white garments, setting the scene in 1890s Texas. This introduction suggests an epic journey is about to unfold. However, the review notes that the subsequent narrative fails to match this initial promise in terms of suspense, emotional impact, or grandeur. The potential tension of the sisters’ dangerous gambit is diminished when their gun-wielding crime spree, which involves robbing various targets, is presented as a quick montage rather than a sustained dramatic sequence.

Critics describe the production as “dismayingly tame” despite its dynamic subject matter of marginalized people asserting themselves in a repressive era. The review characterizes the work as a generic crime musical that lacks outlaw grit and is underserved by superfluous showboating. While the current New York staging is noted to be more muscular than the 2024 production at New Jersey’s Paper Mill Playhouse, it still falls short of the intensity suggested by its premise.
summary: The musical 'Wanted' at the James Earl Jones Theatre in New York City is criticized for being a generic crime production that lacks outlaw grit. The review describes the show as underserved and tame, noting that its dynamic subject matter is diminished by superfluous showboating and a montage sequence that saps tension.

title: Ganbatte: Jairo Alvarez's Photo Series on Japan's Salarymen at Head On Festival 2026
content: Copenhagen-based Argentinian visual artist Jairo Alvarez presents his photographic series Ganbatte, which explores the juxtaposition and harmony between Japan’s relentless work culture and its traditions, connection to nature, and faith. content: With the issues raised in Cape Town still to be resolved, Usman Khawaja’s book threatens to damage reputations and divide cricket’s tight community Australian cricket thought it had left its great shame behind, burying it in the days after Cameron Bancroft was shown on the big screen in Cape Town putting sandpaper down his pants. title: Manchester City's Kerstin Casparij: Football is my most important secondary thing in life
content:
Dutch full-back Kerstin Casparij has discussed the importance of maintaining perspective while navigating the pressures of professional football. Speaking ahead of Manchester City’s upcoming match against Inter in Milan, the player described football as her “most important secondary thing in life,” a viewpoint she finds refreshing. While she admits that losing results in a terrible day, she emphasizes that her family and friends are healthy and she has no financial worries, such as getting food on the table.

Casparij noted that this broader perspective helps her remain the person she has always been. The Dutch international also expressed relief at winning the Double and highlighted the need for a “sense of normality” while living in the public spotlight. She stated that she loves the sport, particularly Champions League nights under the lights, but believes in keeping her priorities balanced.
summary: Kerstin Casparij describes football as her most important secondary thing in life, a perspective that helps her maintain normalcy while in the spotlight. She discusses finding relief from winning the Double and the importance of keeping a healthy balance with family and friends.

title: Felix Nmecha denies goal celebrations promote intolerance
content:
Borussia Dortmund and Germany midfielder Felix Nmecha has responded to criticism regarding his goal celebrations, stating they have been misunderstood and do not promote “intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form.” The Dortmund official supporters’ group criticized Nmecha over the weekend for using a gesture associated with the “The King’s Return” campaign, which is linked to Ballers in God (BIG), a network of Christian football players. Nmecha, a devout Christian, clarified that the gesture is not intended to foster division.

The German public broadcaster ARD has connected BIG to ultra-conservative positions on issues including homosexuality and transgender identity. In reply to the backlash, Nmecha emphasized that the message behind the celebration is one of love, countering claims that the actions promote negative sentiments.
summary: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha stated that his goal celebrations linked to the Ballers in God network are not intended to promote intolerance or hate. He responded to criticism from a supporters' group regarding gestures tied to the "The King's Return" campaign.

title: Trump Proposes UFC CEO Dana White as White House Press Secretary
content: Sport has long been regarded as great unifier but there is evidence that this era of hyper-partisanship may change that Over the weekend, President Trump floated his latest wild idea: that the man behind the Ultimate Fighting Championship and Power Slap, the ethically dubious “sport” where competitors take turns smacking each other with an open palm, could be his new White House press secretary. Trump’s post on Truth Social was about as subtle as a slap to the face. He Trump wanted the UFC chief executive, Dana White, whom he hailed as a “violent Fighter and Warrior”, to take the job. And for six of his fighters to join him “to defend us against the Lunatic Left”. But it also carried a certain logic. The UFC is Maga’s sport of choice. Why couldn’t it also be its praetorian guard?

title: 72-Hour Rugby Broadcast Blitz: Ireland and England Shine, South Africa Ominous
content: A 72-hour TV blizzard was a test of sofa stamina as Ireland and England shone while South Africa looked ominous By Sunday night one question swamped all else. When does a diet of endless televised rugby become too much of a good thing? People are well used to three consecutive Six Nations games on “Super Saturday” but the weekend was on a whole new level. It must have ranked among the most relentless 72-hour blizzards of rugby broadcasting in the game’s history. The Breakdown, naturally, was keen to get among it. Friday night’s Ireland v Argentina game on ITV had its moments, happily, although not as many as England A v Argentina on YouTube. On Saturday, with South Africa 45-0 up against Italy by half-time, there was a case for covering the screen with a Turin shroud. Either way it was time for the haka in Murrayfield before Scotland v New Zealand, subsequently interspersed with an absorbing Champ game between Cornish Pirates and Richmond on Clubber TV.
summary: The weekend featured a 72‑hour rugby broadcast marathon, with Ireland and England performing strongly, while a haka was performed in Murrayfield before Scotland v New Zealand. South Africa led Italy 45‑0 by half‑time, and other matches included England A vs Argentina on YouTube and a Clubber TV game between Cornish Pirates and Richmond.
