title: Curiosity Drills 49th Hole 'Nazca' on Sol 5050
content: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 3 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5050-5055: It’s Nazca, Our 49th Drill Hole This image of the Nazca drill hole was taken by Mast Camera (Mastcam) onboard NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity on Sol 5050 (2026-10-20 23:56:20 UTC). NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Susanne P. Schwenzer, Professor of Planetary Mineralogy at The Open University, UK Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 23, 2026 As regular readers of this blog will know, we returned to the area where we found disc shaped inclusions in the rocks, which we interpreted as potential crystals. If they are indeed crystals, and we compare them to Earth, they could be very interesting indicators of the environmental conditions. Hence, the excitement in the team is high that we found a good block to drill. Good means first and foremost that it contains abundant potential crystals, but of course there is more before we drill. We passed the rover’s stability test, as all wheels have to be on solid ground before we extend the arm. Then we passed the preload test, which tests the stability of the rock and the forces the arm experiences when the drill bit presses into the rock. With all those tests passed, we successfully drilled our 49th drill hole, called “Nazca.” The drill campaign comes with many investigations before and after the drilling itself. Before the drill, we investigated the block with APXS, MAHLI and ChemCam – all on the target Nazca. After drilling, the sample was dropped off to CheMin, with the results still making their way from Mars to Earth. They are eagerly anticipated to reach us over the coming weekend. ChemCam obtained both passive spectral and active LIBS of the tailings and a LIBS measurement down the drill hole wall. Other ChemCam activities this week included a LIBS investigation of “Palpala,” which is a dark pebble. We are on the lookout for those pebbles for a while and find that not all of them have the same composition. To make sure we understand their origin, we are measuring them when there are some in reach that are big enough. If a pebble is too small, it can move when it is being hit by the laser. Hence, we need to look out for some that are big enough. Another such pebble was the target “Puna” identified in Friday’s planning. ChemCam LIBS on the target “Llama” is to get another depth profile to check whether our observations in the first such depth profile are consistently observed or whether they vary between locations. The target “Pacaya” is another measurement of the disc shaped forms that drew us back to this region. In addition to the LIBS measurements, ChemCam has several long distance RMIs in the plan. They are all focused on the two buttes that have drawn a long-standing interest of the team for the various sedimentary structures and textures they reveal: Mishe Mokwa and Cordillera. title: Curiosity Blog: Sols 5056-5062 Focus on Power Recharge Ahead of Nazca Drilling
content: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 3 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5056-5062: Charging Back Up! This image was taken by Right Navigation Camera onboard NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity on Sol 5062 (2026-11-02 05:40:15 UTC). NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS By Remington Free, Operations Systems Engineer, NASA-JPL Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 30, 2026 Today’s plan covered 3 sols, 5060, 5061, and 5062, as we take a few recharging sols before getting back to our normal drilling activities. As you may know if you have been following the blog closely, we are in the middle of a drilling campaign on our target called “Nazca.” We’ve already drilled the hole, characterized the tailings from the drill hole with ChemCam, and have now done several sample dropoffs, both to our SAM and CheMin instruments within the belly of the rover. We still have a number of activities left to do as part of the campaign, including another dropoff to SAM for a different kind of analysis, and drilling cleanup activities. One of those activities is called “RAGE” (Rotate to Agitate for Granule Expulsion, a very fun acronym) where we essentially shake the drill to get any remaining sample out of it. We’ll also make sure to take lots of imaging to continue document the drill hole and tailings. In any case, those activities are very power-hungry for our rover! So today’s plan purposefully did not have a lot of activities in it so we could get a nice few power positive sols before we get back to drilling. Each of our three sols had a standard morning science block, with an extra exciting brand-new activity on 5061 (more on that shortly!). Over the three sols, we conducted remote science with ChemCam active and Remote Micro-Imager mosaics on some interesting targets (“Titicaca,” “Pampas,” and “Salta”), some Mastcam imaging of our calibration target and our drill target, several Navcam dust devil studies and Mastcam tau observations, and twilight imaging. Despite this plan being recharging/waiting, we got in lots of exciting science to continue to study the Nazca crystal formations and the nearby layered rocks and bedrock. On 5061, we also conducted a brand-new engineering activity to test parallelism over one of our downlink communications windows. As the rover gets older and our power output slowly decreases over the length of the mission, we are continuously looking for new ways to execute activities with less power use. One of our strategies is parallelism – having two activities execute at the same time will save power due to the rover being awake for less time. However, we need to vet pairs of activities ahead of time to ensure they are safe to run together. This is a test of one of those pairs – running our CheMin “Get Data” activity at the same time as we are sending data to one of our orbiters. CheMin Get Data is a high CPU activity which transfers science data from the instrument to our flight computers. The test seems to have gone well, but we’ll have to wait to hear back from our engineering team to analyze the results! Overall, it was an exciting plan full of great remote science as we wait to be able to wrap up our drill campaign. Stay tuned to hear more about how the rest of the Nazca campaign went! title: David Ellison: AI Could Be Biggest Creative Unlock in Modern History
content:
During Paramount Skydance’s latest earnings call, CEO David Ellison noted that it is “hard to imagine” AI will fail to have a larger impact on the film industry than CGI. He said the company is looking closely at AI’s potential in production, describing it as “the biggest creative unlock in modern history.”

Ellison compared the current AI wave to the advent of CGI and digital composites in the early 1990s, a technology that enabled landmark films such as Jurassic Park and Terminator 2. He emphasized that AI is likely to surpass that earlier breakthrough in significance.

title: Iain Kay Builds 'Ram-Altman' Script After Sam Altman's Podcast RAM Remarks
content:
A developer named Iain Kay has released a satirical script called Ram‑Altman that lets users email OpenAI CEO Sam Altman once a day whenever their computer reports that more than ten percent of its system RAM is available. Kay describes the project as a “parody project” created in response to Altman’s recent remarks about memory usage on personal PCs.

Altman’s comments came during the October 29 episode of the Cheeky Pint podcast, which featured Stripe President John Collison. In the episode Altman said, “A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center. But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5 percent of the time.”

After the remarks went viral, Altman clarified that his comments were taken out of context and briefly changed his display name to “RAM Altman” on X. Kay notes on the project’s GitHub that the name “objectively excellent” and that the project derives its title from Altman’s temporary handle.
summary: Iain Kay Builds 'Ram-Altman' Script After Sam Altman's Podcast RAM Remarks.
author: Ars Technica

title: Washington bettor who lost $308,000 sues Kalshi over alleged illegal online gambling
content:
A Bellevue, Washington resident, Scott Bright, has filed a lawsuit against KalshiEX LLC, claiming the prediction‑market platform violated Washington’s ban on online gambling. Bright says he lost more than $308,000 on sports wagers placed through Kalshi when such wagering was unlawful in the state. The suit, filed on September 24 in King County Superior Court, seeks a payment of over $580,000.

Bright’s complaint notes that his wagering occurred at a time when the Washington Attorney General had already sued KalshiEX in the same court, alleging the company’s activities violated state gambling laws. Kalshi has responded by filing a motion to dismiss the lawsuit.

The case is being watched by state attorneys general across the United States, many of whom are attempting to shut down Kalshi for alleged violations of state gambling statutes. Bright’s action may test whether unsuccessful gamblers can obtain restitution from the company through individual legal claims.
summary: Scott Bright, a Bellevue, Washington resident, lost over $308,000 making sports wagers on Kalshi and filed a lawsuit on September 24 in King County Superior Court alleging the platform violated Washington’s ban on online gambling. Bright is seeking over $580,000 in damages, and Kalshi has filed a motion to dismiss the case.
author: Ars Technica

title: James Gunn and Peter Safran step down as DCU co-CEOs, Jeremy Latcham to replace them
content:
James Gunn and Peter Safran have announced that they are stepping down as co‑CEOs of the rebooted DC Universe, just two months after the Paramount and Warner Bros. merger. The joint statement from the pair does not specify whether the departure is a resignation or a forced exit, and it offers no details about the future of their planned slate of projects beyond the post‑production film Superman: Man of Tomorrow, slated for 2028.

Producer Jeremy Latcham, identified in the announcement as a protégé of Marvel executive Kevin Feige and a former collaborator with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy and other MCU films, will assume the co‑CEO role. In their statement, Gunn and Safran reflected on four years of work to unite DC under a single creative vision, citing achievements such as restoring Superman to a central position and launching new film and television stories including Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface.

The announcement notes that DCU fans are mourning the news and its potential impact on the franchise. The author of the piece expresses mixed feelings, describing the rebooted DCU films released so far as “enjoyable but rather forgettable,” while praising the television offerings. Specific series highlighted include HBO’s Peacemaker, the Lanterns series, and the upcoming Jimmy Olsen series The People v. Gorilla Grodd, described as a “mockumentary crime comedy superhero series.” The author also mentions that Clayface debuted to good reviews and a solid box‑office showing.
summary: It's barely been two months since the controversial Paramount and Warner Bros. Merger, and we've already got a shockingly unexpected ouster : Co-CEOs of the rebooted DC Universe, James Gunn and Peter Safran, are stepping down from that role despite the Hollywood rumor mill assuming that the duo would be safe.
author: Ars Technica

content: Wyndham left a hardcoded credential in its customer app, which permits anyone to access customer data. The hotel chain declined to confirm whether it can determine if any unauthorized access occurred in the past.

title: Nvidia board considers Jensen Huang's future after co‑founder's alleged spy affair
content:
Jensen Huang, who co‑founded Nvidia in 1993 and has served as its public face for more than three decades, has seen his image questioned after a scandal involving a co‑founder’s alleged affair with a Chinese spy. The episode has placed Nvidia’s board in a position where it must consider how to respond to the situation.

Huang built Nvidia into a multitrillion‑dollar chipmaker and has kept the firm closely tied to his family. His children, Madison and Spencer, hold leadership positions at the company, while his wife, Lori Mills Huang, heads the family foundation that, as of 2024, controls over 60 million Nvidia shares.
summary: Nvidia board considers Jensen Huang's future after co‑founder's alleged spy affair.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Beijing agent sparks US security concerns
content: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang disclosed on Sunday that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be working for Beijing. The revelation has placed the relationship under intense scrutiny, especially given Huang’s close ties to the U.S. president. Footage from a Taipei venue last year shows a hand on the back and a kiss on the cheek between the two, a scene that now carries new significance after the admission.

title: Trump defends Pete Hegseth, backs Jensen Huang as FBI probes spy claim
content: Donald Trump defended defense secretary Pete Hegseth, who is facing an impeachment resolution from Republican senator Thomas Massie, saying Hegseth 'won two wars'. The president, who said he had spoken to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said he was 'amazed' by claims Huang conducted an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and that the FBI was now looking into the issue Jensen Huang’s image has been shattered. Could he be pushed out at Nvidia? Republican Thomas Massie moves to force vote to impeach Pete Hegseth
summary: Trump defends Pete Hegseth, backs Jensen Huang as FBI probes spy claim.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Russia HIV spreads to general population in 27 regions, Rospotrebnadzor says
content: Rospotrebnadzor data shows HIV is spreading beyond risk groups in 27 Russian regions. The virus now circulates among the entire population, with people often unknowingly transmitting it to others.
summary: Rospotrebnadzor data indicate that HIV is spreading among the entire population in 27 Russian regions, not only among risk groups. People are increasingly transmitting the virus to one another, often without knowing they are infected.
author: Euronews

title: Trump says US has won Iran war; Rubio says talks show no progress
content: President Donald Trump declared that the United States has “won” the Iran conflict, noting that new U.S. strikes would be unlikely unless Tehran fails to reach a deal. He cited recent U.S. forces striking Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran responded by demanding Washington lift sanctions and the blockade before any talks, while Senator Marco Rubio reported no progress in negotiations.
summary: The US president said that renewed strikes were unlikely unless Tehran failed to reach a deal, as US forces struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said Washington must end sanctions and the blockade before any talks, while Rubio reported no progress.
author: Euronews

title: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya as delegates arrive amid energy challenges
content: Delegates have arrived in Antalya to begin the United Nations COP31 climate summit, which opened after a year of deadly heatwaves and devastating floods. Attendees confront new challenges, including the war in Iran that is disrupting global energy supplies.
summary: The United Nations COP31 climate summit opened in Antalya after a year marked by deadly heatwaves and devastating floods. Delegates face fresh challenges as the war in Iran disrupts global energy supplies.
author: Euronews

title: Poland's President and Prime Minister honor six victims of Kraków shooting
content: Poland’s President and Prime Minister set aside their political differences to honour the six victims of a deadly shooting in Kraków. The two leaders laid candles and knelt together at a vigil held in the city’s historic centre.
summary: Poland's President and Prime Minister set aside their political differences to honour the six victims of a deadly shooting in Kraków. They laid candles and knelt together at a vigil in the historic city centre.
author: Euronews

title: Explosion at Habaş steelworks in Aliağa kills 17
content: A devastating explosion at the Habaş iron and steelworks in Aliağa, western Turkey, killed 17 people. Witnesses described an earthquake‑like blast, and footage shows flames, thick smoke and distressed relatives outside the factory.
summary: A devastating explosion at the Habaş iron and steelworks in Aliağa, western Turkey killed 17 people. Witnesses said the blast sounded like an earthquake, and video showed flames, thick smoke and distressed relatives outside the factory.
author: Euronews

title: South Africa ANC records worst local election result with 30% vote
content:
South Africa’s ruling ANC suffered its worst‑ever local election results, securing just 30 % of the vote, as coalition talks loom.  

Former Ugandan military intelligence officer Herbert Matanda Mabonga accuses the army of secretly detaining and torturing opponents, following the release of videos that sparked national outrage.  

In Senegal, more than 200,000 free tickets are giving young people the chance to experience the games live on home soil, in a bid to inspire a new generation of athletes.
summary: South Africa's ruling ANC won only 30% of the vote in local elections, its worst ever, prompting coalition talks. Former Ugandan military intelligence officer Herbert Matanda Mabonga alleges the army is secretly detaining and torturing opponents, and Senegal is offering more than 200,000 free tickets to youth to attend the games.
author: France 24

title: UK author M. John Harrison wins Booker Prize for AI‑tinged apocalyptic novel
content: UK author M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday for his novel The End of Everything. The book, described as enigmatic, offers a darkly satirical view of post‑apocalyptic Britain while echoing concerns about artificial intelligence.
summary: M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday for his novel "The End of Everything". The book is an enigmatic, darkly satirical depiction of post‑apocalyptic Britain that echoes concerns about artificial intelligence.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang sued in class action over alleged Chinese spy ties
content: Nvidia ⁠and ​Chief ​Executive Jensen Huang were ​sued ‌on ⁠Monday ‌in ⁠a proposed class ​action accusing ‌them of ‌defrauding ​shareholders by concealing Huang's ties ​with ​a ​suspected ​Chinese spy. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Steve Tsang, Director of the SOAS China Institute, says that the affair "can also be about effectively lobbying Jensen Huang to lobby the US government, because he is a very powerful figure, particularly during the Trump administration, and he, for whatever reason, has been taking a position that is beneficial to Chinese development and advancement of its AI capacity".
summary: Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang sued in class action over alleged Chinese spy ties.
author: France 24

title: French Foreign Minister blames Iran Revolutionary Guards for supermarket fridge cyberattack
content: French Foreign Minister Jean‑Noël Barrot said on Monday that Iran’s Revolutionary Guards were responsible for a recent cyberattack targeting French supermarket refrigerators. He warned that France would impose consequences on Iran for the incident.
summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind a recent cyberattack on French supermarket fridges. He warned that there would be consequences for the country.
author: France 24

title: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces impeachment vote after Massie files articles
content:
A Republican lawmaker moved on Monday to impeach U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, creating the prospect of a congressional vote this week. The action comes days after President Donald Trump’s party experienced a crushing midterm defeat.

Kentucky Congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment, alleging that Hegseth illegally waged war without congressional authorization and abused his powers as Pentagon chief. The development was reported by France 24’s Fraser Jackson from Washington.
summary: A Republican lawmaker moved Monday to impeach US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting up a potentially explosive vote in Congress. Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment accusing Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia shares fall as board investigates CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy affair
content: Nvidia shares slid after the board began probing CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged affair with a businesswoman described as part of a suspected Chinese intelligence operation. The scrutiny has rattled investors, causing the stock to tumble.
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under board scrutiny after reports he was targeted in a suspected Chinese intelligence operation involving a businesswoman with whom he was having an affair. The controversy has rattled investors, causing Nvidia shares to tumble.
author: France 24

title: Amnesty International urges El Salvador and Haiti to reveal troop deployment agreement
content: Amnesty International has urged both El Salvador and Haiti to disclose the agreement that underpins the deployment of roughly 2,000 Salvadoran troops to Haiti, a nation described as gang‑plagued. The organization warns that keeping the terms secret could jeopardize human‑rights protections and accountability.
summary: Amnesty International has called on El Salvador and Haiti to make public the agreement governing the deployment of around 2,000 Salvadoran troops to Haiti. The organization warned that the deployment poses risks to human rights and accountability.
author: France 24

title: Abu Dhabi trilateral talks on Ukraine war face security guarantee deadlock
content: New trilateral talks on the Ukraine war are set to take place in Abu Dhabi. The most recent meeting between Ukrainian and Russian representatives occurred in February, and the same core disagreements persist: Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, a condition Russia regards as a non‑starter.
summary: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which Russia considers a non‑starter.
author: DW World

title: Over half of England headteachers consider leaving early after new Ofsted inspection
content:
A recent poll of school leaders in England found that almost two‑thirds of respondents believe the new Ofsted inspection regime is far more intense than the previous framework.  

The same survey, conducted after schools were inspected under the new system, revealed that more than half of headteachers are considering shortening their careers because of the experience. When asked whether the inspection had affected how long they intend to stay in their role, 52 % said they were thinking of leaving their job sooner than originally planned.
summary: Almost two-thirds of school leaders say the new Ofsted regime is much more intense than the previous framework. 52% of headteachers who responded said they were thinking of leaving their job sooner than planned.
author: Guardian World

title: Gaza landslide kills five, crushes tents as witnesses try to rescue family
content:
Witnesses said they scrambled to rescue three members of a family who were buried after a sand‑bank collapsed in Gaza. The collapse was attributed to high winds and heavy rain, according to their accounts, and the effort to free the victims was described as frantic.

The sand bank, which overlooked a camp for displaced families south of Deir al‑Balah, gave way on Sunday. The landslide killed five people and crushed at least three tents.
summary: A sand bank overlooking a camp for displaced families south of Deir al‑Balah collapsed on Sunday after high winds and heavy rain, killing five people and crushing at least three tents. Witnesses said they frantically tried to rescue three members of a family buried by the landslide.
author: Guardian World

title: Polish prosecutors say it's too early to label Kraków gunman as politically motivated
content:
Polish prosecutors said there is currently no evidence linking the 24‑year‑old suspect who killed six people and wounded 16 in a market‑square shooting in Kraków to any political ideology, and that it is “too early” to determine a motive. The authorities will continue a terrorism investigation into the attack.

The suspect died early Monday in hospital after being critically injured during a shootout with police who attempted to apprehend him following the Saturday assault in the city’s busy market square.
summary: Polish prosecutors say they have no evidence linking the 24‑year‑old Kraków gunman, who killed six people and injured 16 in a market‑square shooting, to any political ideology. The suspect died in hospital early Monday after being wounded in a shootout with police during his arrest.
author: Guardian World

title: MP Chris Ward urges Andy Burnham to drop Labour’s Brexit red lines for closer EU ties
content:
MP Chris Ward, identified as a co‑author of Keir Starmer’s Brexit “red lines”, has urged Labour leader Andy Burnham to abandon those pledges at the next election. Ward argues that discarding the red lines and pursuing a closer relationship with the EU would protect the United Kingdom from global threats.

The appeal follows former chancellor Rachel Reeves, who said it was appropriate for Burnham to consider re‑joining the EU. Ward’s statement adds another call from a senior figure in Starmer’s administration for a faster transition toward a far closer European partnership.
summary: MP Chris Ward urges Andy Burnham to drop Labour’s Brexit red lines for closer EU ties.
author: Guardian World

title: Sydney teen who planned terror attack says he was radicalised online and used ChatGPT
content: Boy says he was first exposed to extremist material on TikTok, turned to Telegram and YouTube for bomb-making instructions, and used ChatGPT to devise his plans Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A teenager who admitted to planning a terrorist attack in Sydney in 2024 has told the court he was radicalised online after first seeing extremist material on TikTok and used ChatGPT to form his plans. The 16-year-old, known under the pseudonym as RK due to his age, pleaded guilty to acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. In a sentencing ruling on Monday, he avoided jail time, with the New South Wales supreme court ordering him into a three-year community corrections order.
summary: The 16-year-old, identified by the pseudonym RK, pleaded guilty to preparing a terrorist act after being radicalised on TikTok and seeking bomb‑making instructions on Telegram and YouTube. The New South Wales Supreme Court sentenced him to a three‑year community corrections order, avoiding jail time.
author: Guardian World

title: Qantas to cut 850 Australian jobs and outsource work to India in AI overhaul
content:
Qantas announced an agreement with Accenture as part of an AI‑driven overhaul, with CEO Vanessa Hudson describing the move as occurring amid “unprecedented” technological disruption. The airline said it will cut 850 Australian jobs and outsource the associated work to India.

The restructuring marks the third major layoff plan announced in Australia within three weeks, following similar moves reported by design company Canva and National Australia Bank.
summary: Qantas announced an agreement with Accenture as it prepares to cut 850 Australian jobs and outsource work to India in an AI‑driven overhaul. The layoff is the third major corporate restructuring announced in Australia in three weeks, following moves by Canva and National Australia Bank.
author: Guardian World

title: Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell dies at 54 after illness
content: Tasmanian premier leads tributes for Russell, who earlier this month returned home to ‘see out his days’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor Todd Russell has died aged 54 after recently announcing deteriorating health. The Tasmanian premier, Jeremy Rockliff, led the tributes on Tuesday morning, saying his thoughts were with Russell’s loved ones.
summary: Todd Russell, a survivor of the Beaconsfield mine collapse, died at age 54 after recently announcing deteriorating health. Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff led tributes on Tuesday morning, saying his thoughts were with Russell’s loved ones.

title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates outdoor Mass in Buenos Aires, millions gather
content: Millions gathered on the streets of Buenos Aires to welcome Pope Leo XIV, who celebrated an outdoor Mass in the Argentine capital. The ceremony marked the second stop of his 12‑day Latin American tour, taking place three weeks after he underwent surgery for lung cancer.
summary: Millions filled the streets of Buenos Aires as Pope Leo XIV celebrated an outdoor Mass in Argentina's capital. The Mass was the second stop of his 12‑day Latin America tour, occurring three weeks after his lung‑cancer surgery.

title: Dana White turns down Trump's offer to become White House press secretary
content: In a social media post over the weekend, the president asked the UFC boss to take over the role, but later said he was "having a little fun".
